## Before you upgrade

- **Docker quick start: back up OpenSearch first.** The quick start now runs OpenSearch 3.9. Your 2.17 data starts on 3.9 without any steps, but it can't go back to 2.17 afterwards. Stop Signalith and copy the data volume first:

  ```sh
  docker compose -f deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml stop
  docker run --rm -v docker_opensearch-data:/data -v "${PWD}:/backup" alpine tar czf /backup/opensearch-data-2.17.tgz -C /data .
  ```

  To stay on 2.17 for now, see [Moving to OpenSearch 3.x](https://signalith.io/docs/opensearch-security/#moving-to-opensearch-3x). Package installs keep the OpenSearch you run; Signalith works with 2.x and 3.x.
- **New ports: 9000 for the web page, 7779 for agents.** New installs and the Docker quick start open the web page and API on `https://localhost:9000`, and agents send to their own port, 7779. An upgraded server keeps its web port and keeps taking data from agents set up earlier, logging a warning for each one, until you set `server.agent_listen`. Reinstall agents from **Add data** to move them to 7779.
- **The admin chooses their own password.** At the first sign-in with the password Signalith generated, the built-in admin is asked to choose a new one, on upgraded installs too. After that, `signalith initial-password` no longer prints it. If you upgraded a Linux server by replacing only the `signalith` binary, its service file is the old one, so run `sudo signalith initial-password -note` once after the upgrade; package and `install.sh` upgrades do this for you.
- **Dotted names in `eval` and `where` are one field.** A name like `userIdentity.userName` is now one field, as in Splunk's SPL. Before 0.3.0, `a.b` joined the values of `a` and `b`. Change any saved search or custom detection that relied on that to `a . b` (with spaces).
- **Shorter sign-ins.** Sign-ins now end after 1 hour without use and 24 hours in all, even with **Keep me signed in** (the NIST SP 800-63B limits). Both are settings. New passwords are checked against a list of common passwords and can be up to 256 characters; existing passwords keep working.

## What's new

**Sign-in and accounts**
- Single sign-on with OpenID Connect or SAML 2.0, and user provisioning with SCIM 2.0. See [Single sign-on](https://signalith.io/docs/sso/).
- Two-step sign-in with an authenticator app or a passkey, passwordless sign-in with a passkey, and a second check before sensitive changes.
- API tokens expire (90 days by default) and show when they were last used. Read-only tokens for the AI tools server.
- [Multi-tenant mode](https://signalith.io/docs/multi-tenant/): separate tenants, each with its own users and data, on one Signalith, managed under **Settings > Tenants**.
- Audit records are chained and signed, and **Check integrity** on the Audit page reports edited, deleted or missing records.

**Several servers**
- **Add a server** on the Servers page: one line to run on the new computer, for a cluster server, a vulnerability scanner or a network sensor.
- Servers share detections, dashboards, asset and identity lists, settings and one certificate authority. Rolling upgrades one server at a time, cluster key rotation, and drain and remove.
- Load balancer support with the PROXY protocol, and OpenSearch failover across several nodes. See [Adding servers](https://signalith.io/docs/multi-server/).
- Faster intake: more writes to OpenSearch at once, shared fairly between agents and tenants.

**Search**
- Many more SPL commands: `tstats`, `chart`, `streamstats`, `eventstats`, `transaction`, `join`, `lookup`, `inputlookup`, `spath`, `rex` (including `mode=sed`), `foreach`, `mvexpand`, `bin`, `append`, `iplocation`, `replace`, `xmlkv`, `accum`, `delta`, `autoregress`, `fieldsummary`, `transpose`, `filldown`, `trendline`, `addinfo`, `concurrency`, `contingency`, `format` and more, plus JSON, multivalue and statistics functions. See [Query language](https://signalith.io/docs/query-language/).
- Every event has `index` and `source` fields. A search that fails stops only itself, within memory limits.
- [Summary indexes](https://signalith.io/docs/summaries/) make `stats`, `timechart` and `tstats` fast over long time ranges.
- Click a dashboard number or row to see the events behind it.
- [Hunting notebooks](https://signalith.io/docs/hunting-notebooks/) keep a hunt's searches, notes and findings together.
- Describe a detection in plain English, then backtest it against past data before turning it on.

**Data and detections**
- New sources: Microsoft 365, Microsoft Entra ID and Azure, AWS CloudTrail, Google Cloud and Google Workspace audit logs, the Okta System Log, Kubernetes audit logs, GitHub audit logs, Apache and Nginx access logs, and more Windows logs.
- **Add data** walks you through onboarding any other log.
- Network sensor with Zeek and Suricata, installed with one line. See [Network sensor](https://signalith.io/docs/network-sensor/).
- More detections from SigmaHQ and Splunk Security Content, covering cloud, web, network and Windows data.
- Vulnerability scanning: a scanner for each network zone, optional deeper scans with OpenVAS (including credentialed scans with encrypted SSH and Windows logins), and findings ranked with CISA KEV and EPSS.
- [Behavior baselines](https://signalith.io/docs/baselines/) raise risk for first-seen and rare activity.
- Slack and Teams buttons to act on findings and approve playbook steps.
- Two-way [Jira and ServiceNow tickets](https://signalith.io/docs/ticketing/) for cases.
- Compliance: evidence mapped to six frameworks, with exportable reports.
- [Cold storage](https://signalith.io/docs/cold-storage/) keeps old event days searchable from a snapshot repository such as an S3 bucket (OpenSearch 3).

**Security and reliability**
- Archive files can be encrypted.
- The AI features treat text from logs as data, so a crafted log line can't steer them.
- Fuzz tests for every parser of untrusted input, CodeQL, OpenSSF Scorecard and container image scanning in CI.
- A Helm chart for running Signalith on [Kubernetes](https://signalith.io/docs/kubernetes/).
- The Docker image is based on Debian 13 and built with Go 1.27.
